en: The Philippine eagle, also known as the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird and is endemic to the forests of Mindanao.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white flower, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, located in Manila, holds the judicial power to interpret the national constitution.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of Luzon over two thousand years ago.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a distinctive two-step forward and one-step backward dance.
Dr. Fe del Mundo designed an improvised bamboo incubator to provide medical care for infants in rural Philippine areas.
Filipino and English are the two official languages of the Philippines, alongside over a hundred regional languages like Cebuano.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spanish rule on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the Oblation, a statue of a blindfolded nude man, for the University of the Philippines.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan is historically symbolized by neighbors carrying a nipa hut to a new location.
Every Filipino citizen must register to vote in the national and local elections once they reach eighteen years old.
